name: YemSarc: A Multimodal Benchmark Dataset for Sarcasm Detection in Yemeni and Related Arabic Dialects
description: YemSarc is the first multimodal (text, audio, and video) benchmark dataset for sarcasm detection in Yemeni dialectal Arabic and seven additional Arabic dialects. It comprises 630 balanced utterances (315 sarcastic, 315 non-sarcastic) drawn from naturally occurring conversational exchanges across eight Arabic dialects: Mahwiti, Ibbi, Adeni, Sanaani, Dhamari, Saudi, Egyptian, and Taizzi. Each target utterance is paired with its preceding conversational context and is represented across three synchronized modalities: written transcript, audio segment, and video frame sequence. The dataset was constructed from two widely popular Yemeni comedic drama series (Bayt Al-Madaliz and Khuruj Nihai), sourced from their official YouTube channels. Annotation was carried out through a structured three-phase protocol by three expert academic linguists, achieving a final inter-annotator agreement of Fleiss' Kappa = 0.7473. The dataset is released with a fully reproducible, speaker-independent, and statistically audited evaluation pipeline. This dataset is intended for non-commercial academic research purposes, including multimodal sarcasm detection, Arabic dialectal NLP, and social media analysis. The dataset is licensed under CC BY 4.0.
